sources.cite: Meli, McNiece et al. (2019) How Bad Can It Git? Characterizing Secret Leakage in Public GitHub Repositories, NDSS Symposium
sources.finding: First large-scale longitudinal study of GitHub secret leakage: secrets affect 100,000+ repositories with thousands of new unique secrets leaking daily; honeytoken AWS keys posted publicly were exploited in ~30 minutes on average with an 83% chance of use — direct empirical grounding for the 'scraped within minutes' claim.

sources.cite: GitGuardian — The State of Secrets Sprawl 2025 (2024 data)
sources.finding: 23.8 million new secrets were leaked on public GitHub in 2024 (25% YoY increase); 70% of secrets leaked in 2022 remained active years later — grounds the scale-of-problem claim and reinforces why rotation (not deletion) is non-negotiable.

sources.cite: GitHub Blog — GitHub found 39M secret leaks in 2024
sources.finding: 39 million secret leaks detected platform-wide in 2024; ~4.4 million blocked by push protection before reaching repos — the citable scale figure for the Recent Evidence callout.

sources.cite: Edward R. Tufte, The Visual Display of Quantitative Information (data-ink ratio)
sources.finding: Data-ink ratio = proportion of a graphic's ink devoted to the non-redundant display of data; the governing principle is 'above all else show the data,' maximize data-ink and erase non-data-ink — directly supports the section's 'plan the evidence first and the styling last / one number per slide' rule.

sources.cite: Garner, J., Alley, M., Wolfe, K., Zappe, S., & Sawarynski, L. E. (2020). Assertion-Evidence Slides Appear to Lead to Better Comprehension and Recall of More Complex Concepts.
sources.finding: Empirical (ASEE) finding that assertion-evidence slide design (a sentence-headline CLAIM supported by visual EVIDENCE, not bullet lists) improves comprehension and recall of complex concepts — grounds the section's 'lead with the claim, one assertion per slide, evidence beside it' guidance.

sources.cite: Alley, M. (2020). Rethinking the Design of Presentation Slides (assertion-evidence approach).
sources.finding: Originating source for the assertion-evidence slide structure: each slide states a single concise assertion as its headline, supported by visual evidence rather than topic-phrase bullets — supports 'one claim, one piece of evidence, one slide.'

gap: 07.mdx relies on GitHub Pages as the canonical 'link loads for me but 404s for the grader' case (Opening Case line 20, Core Concept line 36, Worked Example line 47) but does not name the current second cause of grader-side 404s: Pages build/propagation delay and Actions-based deploys. A learner who just pushed may run the incognito test too early, see a 404, and wrongly conclude the link is private — or pass the test before the new build is live. Research confirms this failure mode is real and current.

sources.finding: GitHub Pages can publish either by deploying from a branch or via a GitHub Actions workflow (actions/deploy-pages), and you confirm a deployment by reviewing the repository's workflow runs — grounding the callout's 'wait for the build to report success in Actions/Pages settings' guidance.

sources.cite: GitHub community Discussion #61073 — Guide: Troubleshooting 404 errors for GitHub Pages sites; Discussion #49074 — Pages build and deployment queued

sources.cite: Locke & Latham (2002) Building a practically useful theory of goal setting and task motivation: A 35-year odyssey. American Psychologist, 57(9), 705-717
sources.finding: Specific, difficult goals consistently produce higher performance than vague 'do your best' goals; goals direct attention and effort and provide a clear standard against which progress is checked -- directly grounding the 'measurable beats vague' claim.

sources.cite: Gollwitzer (1999) Implementation intentions: Strong effects of simple plans. American Psychologist, 54(7), 493-503
sources.finding: Pairing a goal intention with a concrete if-then plan specifying when, where, and how to act substantially increases the rate of goal attainment -- grounds the section's insistence on a target date and a named proof artifact (the 'when/what' commitment).

sources.cite: van Merrienboer, Kirschner & Kester (2003) Taking the load off a learner's mind: Instructional design for complex learning. Educational Psychologist, 38(1), 5-13
sources.finding: Complex-skill acquisition is supported by sequencing tasks so prerequisite knowledge is established before more demanding tasks, managing cognitive load -- grounds the 'order by prerequisite' claim (e.g., spreadsheet before database query).
